name: _nested_view_from_buffer
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::_nested_view_from_buffer(Tensor(a) self, Tensor nested_size, Tensor nested_strides, Tensor offsets) -> Tensor(a). All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_nested_view_from_buffer(Tensor(a) self, Tensor nested_size, Tensor nested_strides, Tensor offsets) -> Tensor(a). This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns and defines the full contract, including every registered overload, keyword arguments, return values, errors, aliasing and mutation; do not narrow the tests to this one representative signature and never remove tests or adapt reference behavior to fit it. Semantics: the operator builds a zero-copy legacy nested view over the storage of the flat 1-D buffer self, where component i is as_strided(nested_size[i], nested_strides[i], offsets[i]) over that same storage (the buffer's own view storage_offset/stride do not shift the components); nested_size, nested_strides and offsets are all declared as Tensors in the registered schema, are int64 metadata read on the host (the supplied tests build them on CPU), and the supplied alias test asserts the result stores the supplied metadata tensors by identity rather than re-creating them, with nested_size/nested_strides supplied as 2-D int64 tensors and offsets as a flat int64 tensor in the supplied cases. The result is nested with the buffer's dtype and device, aliases the buffer storage without copying payload, and writes through a component land in the shared buffer. The sole default overload returns a single Tensor(a) aliased to self, with no separate .out overload; the supplied negative tests assert the candidate raises RuntimeError/TypeError/NotImplementedError for invalid buffers (non-1-D or nested-tensor), malformed or non-int64 metadata, a non-tensor offsets, and out-of-bounds or negative strides.
